subject: dssd: incorporating existing transects when generating transects for a new survey design

messages.author: 8a11d56fb48fc66a
messages.subject: dssd: incorporating existing transects when generating transects for a new survey design
parts:
Dear all,

I'm using your new R package "dssd" to create a new design for a multi-national aerial survey of harbour porpoises in the western Baltic Sea (MiniSCANS II). I have nine different strata and managed to create a new design and a set of line transects (parallel lines with 10 km spacing) for these strata.
For some strata we already have existing transects from the German national monitoring (see here: https://www.bfn.de/themen/meeresnaturschutz/marines-monitoring/wirbeltiere/schweinswale.html ). For comparison with our previous surveys but also between visual and passive acoustic monitoring methods, we would like to keep these transects for these strata, however, we would need to extend the transects to the North to match the extent of the newly designed (and larger) strata. My question is if this is possible to implement in the package dssd.
I guess what we essentially need is to be able to set the starting point of the transects - which is random at the moment as I understand. If we could use the same starting point as the existing transects and then do the 10 km spacing, we should be able to generate a set of new transects, which fit the extent of the new strata but overlap with the existing transects, right?

I hope my issue becomes clear. Otherwise I'm happy to give more information. Many thanks in advance for your help!

Best
Dominik

---

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] dssd: incorporating existing transects when generating transects for a new survey design
parts:
Dominik

I'm not sure I correctly understand your intention.  If your study area is the western Baltic, then you are not interested in the portions of the monitoring scheme in the North Sea, but rather strata I,J,K,L and O from the figure you cite in your email.

Furthermore, what you are proposing is to maintain the placement of transects in those strata shown in figure for consistency with previous work.  If you are not including random realisations of your design, then I'm not certain that dssd is the tool for the job.  The package dssd is useful for examining properties (such as uniformity of coverage) of various designs; accomplished by repeatedly producing realisations of designs.

If the locations of the transects are fixed (to overlap with existing transects), it sounds as if you only need to use a GIS system to extend the existing transects into your new northerly strata.

To my knowledge, it is not possible to fix positions of transects with dssd .  If I have misunderstood, I apologise.  Please clarify.

Eric Rexstad
Senior Research Fellow, CREEM, Univ. of St Andrews, Charity SC013532
eric.r...@st-andrews.ac.uk
The Observatory, Buchanan Gardens, St Andrews KY16 9LZ

parts:
Hi Eric,

sorry for the misunderstanding. You are right that the study area only concerns the western Baltic, the Belt Sea and the Kattegat. So the areas of interest from the German monitoring scheme actually are the strata I, J, K and L.

The idea was to use the existing strata (I, J, K and L) but just extend transects to cover a larger area. However, there are also several strata which have not existed before and thus need to be designed from scratch. I have attached a map of the currently planned strata. I is now extended northwards and called 'Kiel and Little Belt'. J and K ('Fehmarn' and 'Kadetrinne') have remained the same extent. L (here 'Rugen') has actually been extend towards the east (to meet the management border of this population) and there are no transects existing for this extension bit.

I guess the way forward you suggested is probably the best: Use a GIS system to extend the transects to the north for I, and also to create additional transects in regular spacing towards the east for L. Strata extent and transects for J and K will remain the same. I then need to assume two things: 1) that the coverage has been good for the existing strata and 2) will still be good for the new strata with my manual amendments. Concerning the first assumption I'm pretty confident it has been tested but concerning the second: is this fair to assume? Is there a way to check it?
For the new strata, however, I would then create a new design and assess coverage with dssd.

Best
Dominik

messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] dssd: incorporating existing transects when generating transects for a new survey design
parts:
Thanks for the clarification Dominik.  For your "new" strata (the three Kattegat, Great Belt and Oresund strata), it is straightforward to design those surveys from scratch using dssd .

For "Kiel and Little Belt", your design (transect spacing and orientation) will remain the same as it was for old stratum I.  Stratum "Rugen" also has transect spacing and orientation carried over from your previous work.

The outstanding question, as you stated it is "will (coverage) still be good for the new strata with my manual amendments."  That seems tricky.   If you find properties of the survey unsatisfactory (whatever your definition of satisfactory might be) from an investigation you conduct with dssd, what action will you take?  I get the impression that you intend to use the legacy design in those strata.

Eric Rexstad

messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] dssd: incorporating existing transects when generating transects for a new survey design
parts:
Thanks a lot for your feedback, Eric!

That is indeed a good question. Generally speaking, I think that it makes sense to use the previous design (N-S line transects with 10 km spacing) in terms of environmental gradients but also from practical aspects since the passice acoustic network was designed based on the existing transects. This allows a good spatial overlap between CPOD stations and transects...
One thing we will try is to extend the transects as described before and then calculate the resulting line length. This can then be entered as input for the design in dssd and we can run the coverage simulations. In this way we could assess the coverage and see if it is satisfactory. If not, we obviously need to adjust the survey design. What do you think?

I hope my issue becomes clear. Otherwise I'm happy to give more information. Many thanks in advance for your help!

Thanks for the clarification Dominik.  For your "new" strata (the three Kattegat, Great Belt and Oresund strata), it is straightforward to design those surveys from scratch using dssd .

I then need to assume two things: 1) that the coverage has been good for the existing strata and 2) will still be good for the new strata with my manual amendments. Concerning the first assumption I'm pretty confident it has been tested but concerning the second: is this fair to assume? Is there a way to check it?

Am Donnerstag, 30. April 2020 17:57:19 UTC+2 schrieb Eric Rexstad:

Dominik

I'm not sure I correctly understand your intention.  If your study area is the western Baltic, then you are not interested in the portions of the monitoring scheme in the North Sea, but rather strata I,J,K,L and O from the figure you cite in your email.

Furthermore, what you are proposing is to maintain the placement of transects in those strata shown in figure for consistency with previous work.  If you are not including random realisations of your design, then I'm not certain that dssd is the tool for the job.  The package dssd is useful for examining properties (such as uniformity of coverage) of various designs; accomplished by repeatedly producing realisations of designs.

If the locations of the transects are fixed (to overlap with existing transects), it sounds as if you only need to use a GIS system to extend the existing transects into your new northerly strata.

To my knowledge, it is not possible to fix positions of transects with dssd .  If I have misunderstood, I apologise.  Please clarify.

I guess what we essentially need is to be able to set the starting point of the transects - which is random at the moment as I understand.
